ab_ashlar_ridge_ay_mamasita.approach: The wall is reached from the Miette Hot Springs road, which leaves Highway 16 northeast of Jasper; the viewpoint on that road shows the wall and the line of the approach. Park in the small pullout on the left a short drive beyond the viewpoint. Walk toward the creek, turn left on the trail down along it, and cross it (a fixed rope helps when the water is up). Then follow the steep trail marked with orange tape up to the base of the ridge; the last stretch is through a few cliff bands with some scrambling and bushwhacking. The route starts on a good ledge beside a small pine, a good way right of Good Intentions Bad Habits.

ab_ashlar_ridge_roger_s_lunch_buffet.approach: Take the good trail from the Ashlar parking lot to the last hump below the ridge. The first pitch starts from a little ledge beside the shallow crack that slants left up the face, on its right. The parking is the small pullout past the viewpoint on the Miette Hot Springs road; from it the trail goes down to the creek, crosses it and climbs the steep hill to the ridge.

ab_aspen_beauty_bourgeois.approach: The crag is reached from the Icefields Parkway south of Jasper: turn onto Highway 93A at Athabasca Falls, drive past the falls to Leech Lake, and park in the pullout there or in the small one a little further on, on the left. A well-kept trail leads into the forest to the crag. Walk along the base of the cliff past the first couple of short bolted lines until the routes become clean and taller, with big rocks on the ground below. Bourgeois follows the weakness to a small roof in this first taller sector.

ab_castle_mountain_bastion.approach: Start on the Castle Mountain fire lookout trail, which leaves Highway 1A west of Castle Junction. From the lookout, a trail heads north and up, getting steeper, to a gully; cross it to the east and pick the trail up again. It continues steeply to the bottom of the trail that serves Castle Mountain Hut, where rappel bolts are visible at the top. From there head climbers' left (west) to a bowl-shaped wall; the bolts of the first pitch are easy to spot.
ab_castle_mountain_bastion.descent_text: Walking off is the most direct way down: from the top on the plateau head east toward the Castle Mountain Hut access trail, which has a few short fourth class downclimbing sections and an optional rappel, then retrace the approach to the fire lookout. The route can also be rappelled with a long rope; the first rappel from the top ends at a station partway down the face, off to the side of the last pitch's bolts, and skipping it will stick the ropes. The belay anchors are all fixed.

ab_castle_mountain_the_moat.approach: Take the Rockbound Lake trail from its trailhead just east of Castle Junction on Highway 1A, as far as the turnoff for the Lost Lemon crag. Continue a short way beyond it, then head up and left through forest to a drainage. At the wall the prow of The Moat is obvious; the route starts at its toe, on the lower tier beneath Castles in the Sky.
ab_castle_mountain_the_moat.descent_text: The route ends on the ledge below Castles in the Sky. From there either continue up that route, or traverse the ledge to the right back to the Eisenhower Tower trail: the traverse is a hike on steep ground above the lower cliff band, with bolts along the first stretch for those who want to stay roped, and easier-angled ground after that. Keep high until you can curl around to the base of the first Eisenhower tier on its east side, where the trail starts and leads out.

ab_first_wall_daisy_head_maisey.approach: From the large pullout with an outhouse on Highway 16 northeast of Jasper, take the trail that begins at the end of the pullout farthest from the outhouse. It skirts a pond and climbs a steep hill, then flattens and braids on its way up toward Hidden Valley. Continue to the ladder, climb it, keep to the main trail and bear left at any fork. First Wall is on the left a short walk beyond the ladder. Daisy Head Maisey is the second bolt line: it starts up a pinnacle and heads for the low slab section, then branches right at the top of the slab.

ab_intermediate_slab_blown_away.approach: From the large pullout with an outhouse on Highway 16 northeast of Jasper, follow the Hidden Valley trail past the ladder and First Wall. Beyond First Wall, follow the left-trending trail to a cleared area, which is Intermediate Slab. The slab gets plenty of sun and has top rope routes as well as sport lines.

ab_juno_wall_armagedon.approach: Park in the small roadside pullout with wooden signs for Roche Ronde and Smet, just before the bridge on Highway 16 near the east gate of the park. Cross the road to the blasted cliff face and take the obvious trail up its left side for a few steep metres, then bear onto the faint left branch where the trail first splits (easy to miss). The correct trail follows the crest of a grassy ridge with gentle drop-offs either side and occasional cairns; if the ground still slopes up on your left you are too low. Follow it up to a marked ridge, then up the ridge to a cairn between two small spruce trees, which marks the climbers' trail to the wall. A downward scramble protected by wire ropes comes shortly after, and the foot of the wall is a little beyond it, on your left, where the low first bolts are visible.

ab_kiss_the_sky_wall_bailey_s.approach: From the first Medicine Lake viewpoint on the Maligne Lake road, walk along the far side of the lake from the road to Watchtower Creek, then go up the creek and pick up the trail. The trail ends at a bridge of planks; cross it and you are at the wall. Bailey's follows a weakness slanting left into a crack that faces right, with a small V-shaped roof at the third bolt.

ab_lower_wall_colateral_damage.approach: Park in the round, sandy pullout on the Icefields Parkway south of Jasper, a few kilometres south of the Kerkeslin campground entrance. Behind the pullout a small open field leads to a narrow trail through poplar forest toward Kerkeslin. After the forest the trail steepens; shortly after leaving the aspens take the fork to the left (short cliffs visible ahead mean you have overshot the turn) and follow that trail up a narrow canyon with a creek. The Lower Wall is the first wall on entering the canyon. Colateral Damage is the first route on your left when you enter, alone on the left-hand wall; the others are on the right-hand wall, a little further up.

ab_merlin_wall_merlin_s_warm_up.approach: The wall is visible from Highway 16 near the east gate of the park. A steep path from the lot climbs to the top of the slabs, and the routes are reached by walking along the top of the rock; Aqua Size is the southernmost line on the River Rock section and is the one line there you can walk to without rappelling in.

ab_morro_slabs_river_dance.approach: Use the small parking area on the east side of the second Athabasca River bridge. ab_mount_buller_running_of_the_buller.approach: Park at the large cairn on top of the embankment beside the Spray Lakes road, at the buttress closest to the road. Scramble up the embankment, where a faint climber's trail leads into the trees and joins the High Rockies gravel trail. Turn right along the gravel trail to a talus field with a few cairns, then turn uphill on a faint path with long traversing switchbacks, which becomes more obvious halfway to the wall. Look for the big right-facing corner at the contact between the grey and yellow rock. A flat ledge with two bolts there is a place to gear up, and the route starts a short way below it, usually marked by a small cairn.

ab_mount_hector_and_mount_andromache_ach.approach: Park at the pullout on the west side of Highway 93 in front of Hector Creek. Cross the road and look for the Mount Hector trail, which starts on the south bank of the drainage. It rises through forest along the left edge of an avalanche bowl and ends above a waterfall. Cross the creek there and enter the small hanging valley between Mount Andromache and Little Hector. Follow cairns to a two-tiered tree island, then cairns and goat trails up and left across a series of benches and an easy gully to the upper benches. Cross left (northwest) over a bowl with a large boulder, follow the steps of a dry watercourse up the basin to the base of the towers, and go to the farthest-left bowl rather than around toward the highway. The right-hand tower is easily mistaken for Achilles Spire; the spire has a small crumbly tower on its left, a sharp pointed tower on its right, and narrowing drainages on both sides, with a large black roof beside the right-hand drainage. The route starts below and left of that roof, at a one-bolt station on a small ledge among smaller overlapping overhangs.
ab_mount_hector_and_mount_andromache_ach.descent_text: Rappel the route. The line is set up for rappels from bolted stations, with a few short scrambles on ledges between stations and a walk around the buttress partway down. Some of the rappels run over steep or overhanging rock and the rope pulls with friction, so knot the ends. From the bottom, follow the cairns back down to the trail.

ab_rainy_day_slab_free_diver.approach: From the Maligne Lake Road, a little past the picnic area, look for two boulders on the left. The trail climbs beside a boulder field to the slab. The route starts from trees with flagging tape, some distance south of the corner at the north end of the slab.

ab_rave_cave_pigs_in_space.approach: Park at the pullout at Leech Lake on Highway 93A, south of Jasper past Athabasca Falls, or at the next small pullout beyond it, and follow the maintained trail into the forest to the Lost Boys cliffline. Walk along the cliffline to the very obvious cave formed by a boulder pile, which you can pass under or around, and scramble onto its roof. The route is the left-hand bolt line, starting from the roof of the cave.

ab_rock_gardens_alain_s_route.approach: Park at the pullout for the fifth bridge on the Maligne Lake Road and walk across the bridge, then turn left into the forest toward the sixth bridge. After a minute or so turn right onto trail 7H and climb a steep hill. Where 7H bears right, take the unmarked trail on the left and follow it through open Douglas fir forest. When you see a drop-off on your left you are close: turn right and downhill for the Rock Gardens (continuing left leads to the Boulder Gardens). When you reach the boulder field, angle up and right across it, then keep to the trail beyond three smaller, chossy cliffs until you arrive at the one worth climbing. Inhale Deeply begins on a grubby ledge over Spray some on yourself. The ledge can be reached by walking down or rappelling from the Tastes like Tabasco anchor, by taking a belay from the Spray some on your friends anchor, or by the short ramp on the right. Clip into the bottom anchor, then head up the obvious bolt line toward a dihedral.

ak_bear_spray_wall_tastes_like_tabasco.approach: Walk up alongside the creek, past the culvert, and pick up the flagged trail that heads toward the cliffs. When you reach the boulder field, angle up and right across it, then keep to the trail beyond three smaller, chossy cliffs until you arrive at the one worth climbing. At the wall, follow the ramp up and to the left until you see the bolts.

ak_canwell_crag_gunshot.approach: Drive about halfway through Red Rock Canyon, round the bend where the big red debris pile comes nearest the road, and use any pullout past it. Look east toward the canyon rim for a prominent ridge that reaches the canyon floor with very little bushwhacking, and hike it to the rim. From the west rim, cross the tundra plateau to the east rim, where the alpine lake below Canwell Peak comes into view. The crags are a little south of there, closer to the peak, on top of the plateau. Gunshot takes the crag's steepest ground, left of Power Outage.

ak_the_arboretum_the_arborist.approach: Starting at Spruce cabin, follow the approach trail and scramble over boulders northward to the first beach, going by the first gully that drains Waterfall Tower. Skirt the overgrowth to the second beach and climb the obvious gully that descends from the base of the Apron. The boulder holding the route is in the woods on your right a few minutes up the gully; if you missed it, you are in the wrong gully.

ak_weird_alaska_wall_back_fur.approach: Take the trail up to the boulders. From there you can climb straight to the wall, or bear up and right onto a trail running along the boulder field's right edge, which sidesteps the loose rock and moss and ends at the base of Chest Fur. The routes run to the right from there. Back Fur follows Chest Fur for seven bolts, then goes right before the wide crack. Be careful on the ledge, which has loose rocks and dirt.

ak_weird_alaska_wall_chest_fur.approach: Take the trail up to the boulders. From there you can climb straight to the wall, or bear up and right onto a trail running along the boulder field's right edge, which sidesteps the loose rock and moss and ends at the base of Chest Fur. The routes run to the right from there. Chest Fur is the first route you see on arrival at the wall by the trail.

ak_weird_alaska_wall_sourdough_stories.approach: Take the trail up to the boulders. From there you can climb straight to the wall, or bear up and right onto a trail running along the boulder field's right edge, which sidesteps the loose rock and moss and ends at the base of Chest Fur. The routes run to the right from there. Sourdough Stories is on the next buttress that sticks out, left of where you meet the main wall; there is not a good trail on this stretch.

ak_weird_alaska_wall_unnamed_1.approach: Take the trail up to the boulders. From there you can climb straight to the wall, or bear up and right onto a trail running along the boulder field's right edge, which sidesteps the loose rock and moss and ends at the base of Chest Fur. The routes run to the right from there. This is the second line of bolts, beside the big boulder you reach on arriving at the wall. The start can be on the mossy boulder itself or on the ground beside it, to its left.

ak_weird_alaska_wall_unnamed_2.approach: Take the trail up to the boulders. From there you can climb straight to the wall, or bear up and right onto a trail running along the boulder field's right edge, which sidesteps the loose rock and moss and ends at the base of Chest Fur. The routes run to the right from there. This route is to the right of Chest Fur; it is the left, harder one of a pair of corners that face each other.

ak_weird_alaska_wall_unnamed_3.approach: Take the trail up to the boulders. From there you can climb straight to the wall, or bear up and right onto a trail running along the boulder field's right edge, which sidesteps the loose rock and moss and ends at the base of Chest Fur. The routes run to the right from there. This route is the right, easier one of the two corner routes that face each other.

ak_weird_alaska_wall_unnamed_5.approach: Take the trail up to the boulders. From there you can climb straight to the wall, or bear up and right onto a trail running along the boulder field's right edge, which sidesteps the loose rock and moss and ends at the base of Chest Fur. The routes run to the right from there. This route is downhill and to the left of Dancing in your XtraTufs.

az_notorious_wall_10_crack_commandments.approach: The McNutt climbing area is BLM land along the northern edge of the wilderness, entered through a gate. From the parking area the walls are a short walk up the wash. Notorious Wall is the first area reachable from the parking lot: walk south from the parking area to where the wash changes from a north-south to an east-west course, and use the burro trail alongside the wash. The route climbs a spring runoff at the end of the wall, and the belay is a small cave. Party and Bullshit is the next line along.

az_notorious_wall_big_poppa.approach: The McNutt climbing area is BLM land along the northern edge of the wilderness, entered through a gate. From the parking area the walls are a short walk up the wash. Notorious Wall is the first area reachable from the parking lot: walk south from the parking area to where the wash changes from a north-south to an east-west course, and use the burro trail alongside the wash. Big Poppa takes the tower's right flank, in the gap between Suicidal Thoughts and Ready to Die.

az_notorious_wall_juicy.approach: The McNutt climbing area is BLM land along the northern edge of the wilderness, entered through a gate. From the parking area the walls are a short walk up the wash. Notorious Wall is the first area reachable from the parking lot: walk south from the parking area to where the wash changes from a north-south to an east-west course, and use the burro trail alongside the wash. Walk in toward the wall and stay along the right side of its U-shaped bend; Juicy sits in the gap separating Party and Bullshit from Machine Gun Funk.

az_notorious_wall_machine_gun_funk.approach: The McNutt climbing area is BLM land along the northern edge of the wilderness, entered through a gate. From the parking area the walls are a short walk up the wash. Notorious Wall is the first area reachable from the parking lot: walk south from the parking area to where the wash changes from a north-south to an east-west course, and use the burro trail alongside the wash. Machine Gun Funk is the furthest-left line on the freestanding tower, near Juicy and Ready to Die, and starts with an easy scramble up the main tower.

az_notorious_wall_party_and_bullshit.approach: The McNutt climbing area is BLM land along the northern edge of the wilderness, entered through a gate. From the parking area the walls are a short walk up the wash. Notorious Wall is the first area reachable from the parking lot: walk south from the parking area to where the wash changes from a north-south to an east-west course, and use the burro trail alongside the wash. Party and Bullshit is between 10 Crack Commandments and Juicy and climbs the largest water runout in the area.

az_notorious_wall_ready_to_die.approach: The McNutt climbing area is BLM land along the northern edge of the wilderness, entered through a gate. From the parking area the walls are a short walk up the wash. Notorious Wall is the first area reachable from the parking lot: walk south from the parking area to where the wash changes from a north-south to an east-west course, and use the burro trail alongside the wash. Ready to Die is the central climb on the tower and an easy scramble-like route.

az_notorious_wall_suicidal_thoughts.approach: The McNutt climbing area is BLM land along the northern edge of the wilderness, entered through a gate. From the parking area the walls are a short walk up the wash. Notorious Wall is the first area reachable from the parking lot: walk south from the parking area to where the wash changes from a north-south to an east-west course, and use the burro trail alongside the wash. Suicidal thoughts climbs the tower's west face, the westernmost line on the wall. The start steps from a pointed boulder onto a slightly overhanging crux, and the belay near the base is tenuous.

az_slim_shady_wall_homicide.approach: The McNutt climbing area is BLM land along the northern edge of the wilderness, entered through a gate. From the parking area the walls are a short walk up the wash. Slim Shady Wall is up the draw, along the wash's south bank, ahead of the point where the riverbed bends south. Homicide is the third route from the left.

az_slim_shady_wall_lose_yourself.approach: The McNutt climbing area is BLM land along the northern edge of the wilderness, entered through a gate. From the parking area the walls are a short walk up the wash. Slim Shady Wall is up the draw, along the wash's south bank, ahead of the point where the riverbed bends south. Lose Yourself is the right-most climb on the wall; the start comes out of scattered scree and boulders, so a beta clip helps.

az_slim_shady_wall_my_name_is.approach: The McNutt climbing area is BLM land along the northern edge of the wilderness, entered through a gate. From the parking area the walls are a short walk up the wash. Slim Shady Wall is up the draw, along the wash's south bank, ahead of the point where the riverbed bends south. My Name Is is the second climb from the left.

az_slim_shady_wall_real_slim_shady.approach: The McNutt climbing area is BLM land along the northern edge of the wilderness, entered through a gate. From the parking area the walls are a short walk up the wash. Slim Shady Wall is up the draw, along the wash's south bank, ahead of the point where the riverbed bends south. Real Slim Shady is the left-most, south-most climb and starts with a section to shimmy up between two walls.

az_wu_tang_wall_c_r_e_a_m.approach: The McNutt climbing area is BLM land along the northern edge of the wilderness, entered through a gate. From the parking area the walls are a short walk up the wash. Wu Tang Wall is reached from roughly the midpoint of the access road beyond the gate: go west off the road, cross the riverbed, and climb to the freestanding wall. The development is on the north side. C.R.E.A.M is the middle route on the wall.

az_wu_tang_wall_protect_ya_neck.approach: The McNutt climbing area is BLM land along the northern edge of the wilderness, entered through a gate. From the parking area the walls are a short walk up the wash. Wu Tang Wall is reached from roughly the midpoint of the access road beyond the gate: go west off the road, cross the riverbed, and climb to the freestanding wall. The development is on the north side. Protect Ya Neck is the left-most climb on the north wall; the second pitch starts from a hanging belay.

az_wu_tang_wall_shadowboxin.approach: The McNutt climbing area is BLM land along the northern edge of the wilderness, entered through a gate. From the parking area the walls are a short walk up the wash. Wu Tang Wall is reached from roughly the midpoint of the access road beyond the gate: go west off the road, cross the riverbed, and climb to the freestanding wall. The development is on the north side. Shadowboxin is at the midpoint of the north wall; the lowest belay stands on a sloping bank, with anchors provided there.

bc_ahren_s_rock_faulty_towers.approach: Ahren's Rock is one of the Sunrise Crags, reached by the built trails and stairs that climb from the Crest Lake day-use area. The bolts are plain to see on the rock, and the route starts right above a wooden sign that reads Ahren's Rock.

bc_crow_s_nest_butler_ar_te.approach: Pull in at the Crest Lake day-use area, take the gravel road on the right, and park by the picnic area in the northwest corner of the lake. Cross the highway on foot and follow the trail east for a short distance to reach Crow's Nest. The route climbs the blocky arete with a series of small overhangs.
bc_crow_s_nest_butler_ar_te.descent_text: Rappel from the anchors around the corner to the right, or walk off by climbing a cracked boulder and following the trail down to the right.

bc_joint_wall_karmacide.approach: Joint Wall is reached from the third pullout along the highway to Gold River; a trail descends from there to a rocky riverbed. The route begins up on a low fifth-class ledge, off to the left of the main wall. A side path on the wall's right climbs to the top, where top ropes can be rigged.

bc_lower_hidden_walls_midnight_rider.approach: Leave the car at the day-use area beside Crest Lake, walk over the bridge, and follow the signed trail. Lower Hidden Walls is the first set of climbs you come to. Midnight Rider is a bolted line to the left of Windweaver.

bc_lower_hidden_walls_no_margarine_for_a.approach: Leave the car at the day-use area beside Crest Lake, walk over the bridge, and follow the signed trail. Lower Hidden Walls is the first set of climbs you come to. This is the third route from the left on the ledge.

bc_lower_hidden_walls_snakebite.approach: Leave the car at the day-use area beside Crest Lake, walk over the bridge, and follow the signed trail. Lower Hidden Walls is the first set of climbs you come to. Snakebite is on the slab below the obvious tree with a large root sticking out onto it.

bc_lower_hidden_walls_the_good_the_bad_a.approach: Leave the car at the day-use area beside Crest Lake, walk over the bridge, and follow the signed trail. Lower Hidden Walls is the first set of climbs you come to. This is the second route off the ledge.

bc_lower_sunrise_dancing_madly_backwards.approach: Leave the car at the day-use area beside Crest Lake, walk over the bridge, and follow the signed trail. Follow the signs up toward Sunrise and bear right at the fork near the top to reach Lower Sunrise, a north-facing wall. It takes the bolted face midway across the formation.

bc_middle_hidden_walls_overhead_hazard.approach: Approach through New Crest and follow the signs to the Hidden Walls; Middle Hidden Walls is the second tier of cliffs. The route is the last one on the Middle Hidden Wall before the trail climbs to the Upper Hiddens.

bc_salamander_doubting_thomas.approach: Leave the car at the day-use area beside Crest Lake, walk over the bridge, and follow the signed trail. Follow the signs to Sunrise, and Salamander appears on your left. This is the second route on the wall.

bc_salamander_middle_earth.approach: Leave the car at the day-use area beside Crest Lake, walk over the bridge, and follow the signed trail. Follow the signs to Sunrise, and Salamander appears on your left. Middle Earth starts right of the crack and joins Hobbit Step partway up.

bc_salamander_salamander.approach: Leave the car at the day-use area beside Crest Lake, walk over the bridge, and follow the signed trail. Follow the signs to Sunrise, and Salamander appears on your left. It follows bolts on the face next to the prominent crack of Bitches Brew.

bc_sluice_wall_yellow_ribbon.approach: Access is from the third pullout on the highway toward Gold River. Take the trail down to the rocky riverbed. Sluice Wall lies close to Joint Wall on its right, where a path climbs a few steps. Yellow Ribbon is the second line up the wall and takes the main part of the overhang.
bc_sluice_wall_yellow_ribbon.descent_text: The route has rappel anchors; rappel from them.

ca_brownstone_buttress_a_mine_is_a_terri.approach: Start from the Pine Creek pack station, where the road ends, and hike the Pine Creek Pass trail uphill. The wall shows up on your left almost beside the path, and since the trail is exposed to sun while the wall is shaded, leaving early is wise. Stepping off the trail at its nearest point to the wall puts you at the left side of the broad buttress. The route starts a short way right of Whats Mine Is Mine.

ca_brownstone_buttress_all_mine.approach: Start from the Pine Creek pack station, where the road ends, and hike the Pine Creek Pass trail uphill. The wall shows up on your left almost beside the path, and since the trail is exposed to sun while the wall is shaded, leaving early is wise. Stepping off the trail at its nearest point to the wall puts you at the left side of the broad buttress. The opening is a tricky high step onto grooves and dikes.

ca_brownstone_buttress_brownstone_effect.approach: Start from the Pine Creek pack station, where the road ends, and hike the Pine Creek Pass trail uphill. The wall shows up on your left almost beside the path, and since the trail is exposed to sun while the wall is shaded, leaving early is wise. Stepping off the trail at its nearest point to the wall puts you at the left side of the broad buttress. The route starts left of Whats Mine Is Mine and shares its midway and top anchors.

ca_brownstone_buttress_glory_hole.approach: Start from the Pine Creek pack station, where the road ends, and hike the Pine Creek Pass trail uphill. The wall shows up on your left almost beside the path, and since the trail is exposed to sun while the wall is shaded, leaving early is wise. Stepping off the trail at its nearest point to the wall puts you at the left side of the broad buttress. The route is right of center on the wall, to the right of a prominent roof, and follows an overhanging flake past two large holes.

ca_brownstone_buttress_i_me_mine.approach: Start from the Pine Creek pack station, where the road ends, and hike the Pine Creek Pass trail uphill. The wall shows up on your left almost beside the path, and since the trail is exposed to sun while the wall is shaded, leaving early is wise. Stepping off the trail at its nearest point to the wall puts you at the left side of the broad buttress. The route follows a technical seam up the wall.

ca_brownstone_buttress_inobvious_deposit.approach: Start from the Pine Creek pack station, where the road ends, and hike the Pine Creek Pass trail uphill. The wall shows up on your left almost beside the path, and since the trail is exposed to sun while the wall is shaded, leaving early is wise. Stepping off the trail at its nearest point to the wall puts you at the left side of the broad buttress. It is the farthest-right line on the wall, a two-pitch route whose first pitch has a steep start and mantles.

ca_brownstone_buttress_mine_s_eye.approach: Start from the Pine Creek pack station, where the road ends, and hike the Pine Creek Pass trail uphill. The wall shows up on your left almost beside the path, and since the trail is exposed to sun while the wall is shaded, leaving early is wise. Stepping off the trail at its nearest point to the wall puts you at the left side of the broad buttress. The route climbs a left-facing flake to a high first bolt, then goes up and left to a red iron pocket.

ca_brownstone_buttress_once_upon_a_mine.approach: Start from the Pine Creek pack station, where the road ends, and hike the Pine Creek Pass trail uphill. The wall shows up on your left almost beside the path, and since the trail is exposed to sun while the wall is shaded, leaving early is wise. Stepping off the trail at its nearest point to the wall puts you at the left side of the broad buttress. The route starts below a small pedestal on the right side of the cliff, where an obvious seam splits it.

ca_brownstone_buttress_out_of_our_mines.approach: Start from the Pine Creek pack station, where the road ends, and hike the Pine Creek Pass trail uphill. The wall shows up on your left almost beside the path, and since the trail is exposed to sun while the wall is shaded, leaving early is wise. Stepping off the trail at its nearest point to the wall puts you at the left side of the broad buttress. It shares its opening bolts with the 10d route to its right (Terrible Thing To Waste) before veering left.

ca_brownstone_buttress_tofu_tufas.approach: Start from the Pine Creek pack station, where the road ends, and hike the Pine Creek Pass trail uphill. The wall shows up on your left almost beside the path, and since the trail is exposed to sun while the wall is shaded, leaving early is wise. Stepping off the trail at its nearest point to the wall puts you at the left side of the broad buttress. The route starts left of Glory Hole, crosses it at one shared bolt, and finishes up a golden headwall.

ca_brownstone_buttress_tree_of_the_day.approach: Start from the Pine Creek pack station, where the road ends, and hike the Pine Creek Pass trail uphill. The wall shows up on your left almost beside the path, and since the trail is exposed to sun while the wall is shaded, leaving early is wise. Stepping off the trail at its nearest point to the wall puts you at the left side of the broad buttress. The route is in the middle of the overhanging section, and starts from a good perch.

ca_brownstone_buttress_trouble_in_mine_p.approach: Start from the Pine Creek pack station, where the road ends, and hike the Pine Creek Pass trail uphill. The wall shows up on your left almost beside the path, and since the trail is exposed to sun while the wall is shaded, leaving early is wise. Stepping off the trail at its nearest point to the wall puts you at the left side of the broad buttress. This is the first pitch of Trouble In Mine and climbs dikes to a bulge.

ca_brownstone_buttress_whats_mine_is_min.approach: Start from the Pine Creek pack station, where the road ends, and hike the Pine Creek Pass trail uphill. The wall shows up on your left almost beside the path, and since the trail is exposed to sun while the wall is shaded, leaving early is wise. Stepping off the trail at its nearest point to the wall puts you at the left side of the broad buttress. On the left side of the wall is a large low-angle slab with no routes; the arete right of it is an 11a, and this is the seam just right of that arete.

ca_brownstone_buttress_where_s_the_jam.approach: Start from the Pine Creek pack station, where the road ends, and hike the Pine Creek Pass trail uphill. The wall shows up on your left almost beside the path, and since the trail is exposed to sun while the wall is shaded, leaving early is wise. Stepping off the trail at its nearest point to the wall puts you at the left side of the broad buttress. It lies in the gap separating Tree of the Day from Tofu Tufas, with the first few bolts held in common with Tofu Tufas.

ca_highlands_wall_dr_no.approach: Begin at the Lake George parking area and hike the Crystal Lake trail toward Crystal Crag. The northeast-facing Highlands Wall at the foot of the crag is the first cliff you reach, and it can be seen from the lot. The route starts with a slabby section.

ca_highlands_wall_no_time_to_die.approach: Begin at the Lake George parking area and hike the Crystal Lake trail toward Crystal Crag. The northeast-facing Highlands Wall at the foot of the crag is the first cliff you reach, and it can be seen from the lot.

ca_highlands_wall_riverdance.approach: Begin at the Lake George parking area and hike the Crystal Lake trail toward Crystal Crag. The northeast-facing Highlands Wall at the foot of the crag is the first cliff you reach, and it can be seen from the lot. It begins on the ledge reached by Northeast Buttress's first pitch, or by the pitch of Islay.

ca_highlands_wall_skyfall.approach: Begin at the Lake George parking area and hike the Crystal Lake trail toward Crystal Crag. The northeast-facing Highlands Wall at the foot of the crag is the first cliff you reach, and it can be seen from the lot.

ca_ldr_corridor_south_side_pretty_in_pin.approach: Lower Dinosaur Rock is reached by a good trail from the edge of Campsite 2. Enter the hidden corridor from the east; the south side climbs are on your left. The route is in the center of the corridor, just left of T-Rex.

ca_lime_aid_rinds_of_good_times.approach: From the north shore of Big Bear Lake, park where Greenway Drive meets Pioneer Lane and take the trails that wander up the hillside; the formations sit on the south-facing slope above. Lime-Aid is south of Table Top Rock and a little southwest of Shark Fin; it can be easier to hike straight uphill from the west end of Pioneer Lane. The route starts from a downed log on the left side of the west face.

ca_lime_aid_the_fun_never_ends.approach: From the north shore of Big Bear Lake, park where Greenway Drive meets Pioneer Lane and take the trails that wander up the hillside; the formations sit on the south-facing slope above. Lime-Aid is south of Table Top Rock and a little southwest of Shark Fin; it can be easier to hike straight uphill from the west end of Pioneer Lane. The route goes straight up the center of the west face.

ca_low_tide_wall_alejandros.approach: Park at Lake George and walk around the right side of the lake, then follow the dry creek or the trail on the north side of Crystal Creek. The wall sits just above a huge boulder in the creek that you can see from below; the other way in is to take the Crystal Lake trail, turn left at the lake, and descend to the wall. This is the center route on the wall.

ca_low_tide_wall_cardon.approach: Park at Lake George and walk around the right side of the lake, then follow the dry creek or the trail on the north side of Crystal Creek. The wall sits just above a huge boulder in the creek that you can see from below; the other way in is to take the Crystal Lake trail, turn left at the lake, and descend to the wall. This is the route farthest to the right.

ca_low_tide_wall_negative_tides.approach: Park at Lake George and walk around the right side of the lake, then follow the dry creek or the trail on the north side of Crystal Creek. The wall sits just above a huge boulder in the creek that you can see from below; the other way in is to take the Crystal Lake trail, turn left at the lake, and descend to the wall. This is the farthest left (downhill) route on the wall.

ca_lower_dinosaur_rock_south_face_last_o.approach: Take the good trail from the edge of Campsite 2 to Lower Dinosaur Rock, then skirt along its east side and head west to the foot of the south face. The route starts just right of Better than Dip.

ca_mammoth_crest_cold_winds_of_destiny.approach: Park in the large lot at Horseshoe Lake, at the end of Highway 203, and hike the Mammoth Pass Trail as far as McLeod Lake. Work around the lake shore to its southwest side, where a well-worn path enters the trees, then follow the use trail that climbs the hillside beside a talus slide to the snowfield and talus band beneath the walls of the crest; snow can linger there into summer. The route is the left of the two fully bolted lines on the Ski Tracks Wall.

ca_mammoth_crest_crestfallen.approach: Park in the large lot at Horseshoe Lake, at the end of Highway 203, and hike the Mammoth Pass Trail as far as McLeod Lake. Work around the lake shore to its southwest side, where a well-worn path enters the trees, then follow the use trail that climbs the hillside beside a talus slide to the snowfield and talus band beneath the walls of the crest; snow can linger there into summer. The route is well left of the Requiem Wall, on the right side of an obvious class 2 gully that leads to the rim, beside a big tree; stay low on the approach until directly below the gully.

ca_mammoth_crest_hippie_chick.approach: Park in the large lot at Horseshoe Lake, at the end of Highway 203, and hike the Mammoth Pass Trail as far as McLeod Lake. Work around the lake shore to its southwest side, where a well-worn path enters the trees, then follow the use trail that climbs the hillside beside a talus slide to the snowfield and talus band beneath the walls of the crest; snow can linger there into summer.

ca_mammoth_crest_pain_killer.approach: Park in the large lot at Horseshoe Lake, at the end of Highway 203, and hike the Mammoth Pass Trail as far as McLeod Lake. Work around the lake shore to its southwest side, where a well-worn path enters the trees, then follow the use trail that climbs the hillside beside a talus slide to the snowfield and talus band beneath the walls of the crest; snow can linger there into summer. The route is the right of the two bolted lines on the Ski Tracks Wall.

ca_mammoth_crest_wow.approach: Park in the large lot at Horseshoe Lake, at the end of Highway 203, and hike the Mammoth Pass Trail as far as McLeod Lake. Work around the lake shore to its southwest side, where a well-worn path enters the trees, then follow the use trail that climbs the hillside beside a talus slide to the snowfield and talus band beneath the walls of the crest; snow can linger there into summer.

ca_miracle_revival_dome_killer_good_rout.approach: Hike up to Church Domes; Miracle Revival Dome is the quickest of them to reach. Its west face holds the climbing, and this line sits immediately left of Forgive Me Father.

ca_motherlode_rock_east_face_swing_direc.approach: From the Holcomb Valley Pinnacles northern parking area, a network of trails leads to Motherlode Rock; the east face can also be reached from The Amphitheatre. The route is a direct start to Shantytown Swing from the ground and joins it at the top of the ramp.

ca_motherlode_rock_north_face_here_comes.approach: Start at the northern parking area; the trail runs under the Incinerator Wall and ends at the narrow, shaded north face. The route is a link-up that starts up Short Fuse and finishes on Boom Sauce.

ca_motherlode_rock_west_face_gene_yanamo.approach: From the northern parking area follow the trail that passes beneath the Incinerator Wall, then cut right up the steep rocky gully below the left side of the west face. The route is the second one right of Good Day for a Hangin', beside a pine tree.

ca_north_buttress_2_after_party.approach: Follow the John Muir Trail (the Cathedral Lakes trail) from Tuolumne Meadows; the buttress toe is a very short distance from the trail. After Party begins at the top of Garden Party, so climb that route first.

ca_north_face_3_blue_velvet.approach: Park at the Lake George lot, walk around the left shore of the lake, and climb the climbers trail uphill. Close to where it tops out, bear onto the right fork and cross the talus field to the foot of the north face. The route is the furthest bolted line on the right, just right of Dominatrix, and starts in a prominent undercling right off the ground.

ca_north_face_3_dwp.approach: Park at the Lake George lot, walk around the left shore of the lake, and climb the climbers trail uphill. Bear onto the right fork where it tops out and cross the talus to the main north face; this route is on a lower wall a short way down the talus from it. It climbs the left side of a clean arete just right of Special Fun.

ca_north_face_3_instigator.approach: Park at the Lake George lot, walk around the left shore of the lake, and climb the climbers trail uphill. Close to where it tops out, bear onto the right fork and cross the talus field to the foot of the north face. The route is on the technical face left of Dominatrix.

ca_north_face_3_missing_link.approach: Park at the Lake George lot, walk around the left shore of the lake, and climb the climbers trail uphill. Close to where it tops out, bear onto the right fork and cross the talus field to the foot of the north face. The route is left of the Mongoloid arete, on the east-facing part of the north wall.

ca_north_face_3_north_face.approach: Park at the Lake George lot, walk around the left shore of the lake, and climb the climbers trail uphill. Close to where it tops out, bear onto the right fork and cross the talus field to the foot of the north face. The route takes the far left, slabby arete of the face.

ca_north_face_3_special_fun.approach: Park at the Lake George lot, walk around the left shore of the lake, and climb the climbers trail uphill. Bear onto the right fork where it tops out and cross the talus to the main north face; this route is on a separate cliff a short way down the talus to the west. Of the two bolted lines there, take the left one, up the middle of the face.

ca_north_side_lower_tier_southwest_of_sp.approach: Park where forest roads 2N13 and 2N13D meet and use the climbers trail that climbs the ramp over the gully. The North Side Lower Tier is the first side you see from the road, with a trail leading straight to it. The route is on the slab left of a slanting crack.

ca_north_side_lower_tier_southwest_of_yo.approach: Park where forest roads 2N13 and 2N13D meet and use the climbers trail that climbs the ramp over the gully. The North Side Lower Tier is the first side you see from the road, with a trail leading straight to it. The route is the farthest right slab on the north side, and it shares a top-out with Southwest of Spy.

ca_oneida_lundy_drainage_electric_lundy_.approach: Park at the dam at Lundy Lake and follow the trail that climbs the lake's south shore toward Oneida Lake. The route is on the final prominent buttress on the drainage's right-hand side, reached by talus from the trail; the low-angle upper arete is a key marker. It begins in an alcove with some third- and fourth-class climbing, then two bolts on easy ground gain a pedestal.

ca_oneida_lundy_drainage_gnar_wall_aka_r.approach: Park at the Lundy dam and follow the trail toward Oneida Lake. The climb is on the right-hand skyline, the final big feature before the lake, and begins a short way left of Electric Lundy Land.

ca_pipe_wall_keep_dreamin.approach: Start from the Pine Creek pack station and hike the Pine Creek Pass trail uphill. Pipe Wall lies directly beside the path and is the first of the Brownstone walls you come to. The route starts on the two slab bolts at the toe of the wall, shared with Pipe Dream, and goes straight up the headwall.

ca_pipe_wall_pipe_dream.approach: Start from the Pine Creek pack station and hike the Pine Creek Pass trail uphill. Pipe Wall lies directly beside the path and is the first of the Brownstone walls you come to. It is the leftmost line on the wall, marked by two bolts on a slab at its foot.

ca_pipe_wall_pipe_line.approach: Start from the Pine Creek pack station and hike the Pine Creek Pass trail uphill. Pipe Wall lies directly beside the path and is the first of the Brownstone walls you come to. The route starts at the foot of the wall, a step from the trail.

ca_rectory_south_west_face_blessed_be_th.approach: Hike up to the Church Domes; the Rectory south face is the usual way in to this wall. It begins on the steep, tall part of the wall near its middle, left of the giant horizontal bands, between a tall flake and a small pine.

ca_rectory_south_west_face_children_of_a.approach: Hike up to the Church Domes and to the Rectory. The route is on the west face, right of Going My Way, up obvious bolts.

ca_rocky_hollow_boundaries.approach: Park in the small dirt turnout beside Highway 38 and go straight uphill; the approach is short but steep. Be careful not to knock rocks onto the road. The route is on the right side of the west face and climbs a steep arete before stepping left onto the face.

ca_schoolboy_buttress_bagpipe.approach: From the Lake George parking area take the Crystal Lake trail, turn left at the sign to the lake, go around it and take the climbers trail on the left. Continue past the Kilt Wall to Schoolboy Buttress. The route is the arete at the very left side of the buttress, as you come up and around into an alcove.

ca_schoolboy_buttress_little_schoolboy.approach: From the Lake George parking area take the Crystal Lake trail, turn left at the sign to the lake, go around it and take the climbers trail on the left. Continue past the Kilt Wall to Schoolboy Buttress. The route takes a rounded arete whose first three bolts are in the dish beside it; two harder routes lie to the left and a gear route in a prominent dihedral lies to the right.

ca_schoolboy_buttress_made_in_the_shade.approach: From the Lake George parking area take the Crystal Lake trail, turn left at the sign to the lake, go around it and take the climbers trail on the left. Continue past the Kilt Wall to Schoolboy Buttress. It is the next-to-last line at the far left end of the buttress and climbs a chimney with a roof over it.

ca_schoolboy_buttress_the_dark_crystal.approach: From the Lake George parking area take the Crystal Lake trail, turn left at the sign to the lake, go around it and take the climbers trail on the left. Continue past the Kilt Wall to Schoolboy Buttress. The route is just right of Made in the Shade.

ca_secret_spot_rock_hardstart.approach: From the north shore of Big Bear Lake, park where Greenway Drive meets Pioneer Lane and take the trails that wander up the hillside; the formations sit on the south-facing slope above. Secret Spot Rock is hidden in the trees, a hike directly uphill from Shark Fin. The route is on the right side of the south face, just right of Mr. Friction, and starts from a block on the right.

ca_secret_spot_rock_mr_friction.approach: From the north shore of Big Bear Lake, park where Greenway Drive meets Pioneer Lane and take the trails that wander up the hillside; the formations sit on the south-facing slope above. Secret Spot Rock is hidden in the trees, a hike directly uphill from Shark Fin. The route is in the center of the south face, just right of Dirty Little Secret; start up that route and then move right.

ca_sector_mellow_and_sector_evil_seed_a_.approach: Park at Lake George and hike up the climbers trail to Dike Wall, then keep walking beyond the established north face routes. Sector Mellow is the obvious slab reached first; Sector Evil Seed is a scramble up and around the right side of it. This is the right-hand route on the Sector Mellow wall.

ca_sector_mellow_and_sector_evil_seed_al.approach: Park at Lake George and hike up the climbers trail to Dike Wall, then keep walking beyond the established north face routes. Sector Mellow is the obvious slab reached first; Sector Evil Seed is a scramble up and around the right side of it.

ca_sector_mellow_and_sector_evil_seed_li.approach: Park at Lake George and hike up the climbers trail to Dike Wall, then keep walking beyond the established north face routes. Sector Mellow is the obvious slab reached first; Sector Evil Seed is a scramble up and around the right side of it. This is the left-hand route on the Sector Mellow wall; the first bolt can be hard to spot from the ground.

ca_sector_mellow_and_sector_evil_seed_or.approach: Park at Lake George and hike up the climbers trail to Dike Wall, then keep walking beyond the established north face routes. Sector Mellow is the obvious slab reached first; Sector Evil Seed is a scramble up and around the right side of it. This is the first route on the left of the upper Sector Evil Seed wall.

ca_sector_mellow_and_sector_evil_seed_sa.approach: Park at Lake George and hike up the climbers trail to Dike Wall, then keep walking beyond the established north face routes. Sector Mellow is the obvious slab reached first; Sector Evil Seed is a scramble up and around the right side of it. This is the middle route on the Sector Mellow wall.

ca_sector_mellow_and_sector_evil_seed_st.approach: Park at Lake George and hike up the climbers trail to Dike Wall, then keep walking beyond the established north face routes. Sector Mellow is the obvious slab reached first; Sector Evil Seed is a scramble up and around the right side of it. The route climbs the obvious arete.

ca_shark_fin_arete_you_can.approach: From the north shore of Big Bear Lake, park where Greenway Drive meets Pioneer Lane and take the trails that wander up the hillside; the formations sit on the south-facing slope above. Shark Fin is west of and downhill from Big Bubba. The route takes the left arete on the north face.

ca_shrek_rock_thor_s_revenge.approach: Begin in the Voodoo Garden area and climb northwest along the foot of the Voodoo Garden formation. A gap opens uphill, and Shrek Rock stands there beside a big fallen tree; scramble up through large boulders to its base. The route climbs the obvious overhanging face on the south side.

ca_southwest_side_big_mama_s_bulging_but.approach: Park at the junction of forest roads 2N13 and 2N13D, then hike uphill from the road, weaving through brush, to the southwest side of the formation. It lies on the right side of the main west-facing buttress.

ca_southwest_side_mommy_s_little_monster.approach: Park at the junction of forest roads 2N13 and 2N13D, then hike uphill from the road, weaving through brush, to the southwest side of the formation. The route is the leftmost on the west buttress, starting on blocks above the notch.

ca_southwest_side_napoleon_dynamite.approach: Park at the junction of forest roads 2N13 and 2N13D, then hike uphill from the road, weaving through brush, to the southwest side of the formation. The route follows the middle pillar of the southwest face.

ca_southwest_side_napoleon_syndrome.approach: Park at the junction of forest roads 2N13 and 2N13D, then hike uphill from the road, weaving through brush, to the southwest side of the formation. The route starts at the foot of the right-hand buttress on the southwest side.

ca_spicer_sport_crag_unknown.approach: Park close to the dam and walk carefully to its south side; the north-facing wall is a short way along. Look for drill scars and the anchors at the top. The route is under the highest set of anchors; start directly below and go straight up.

ca_synagogue_unknown_modern_steep_sport_.approach: Hike up to the south face of the Rectory and continue east. The way in stays high past the Rectory south face, with some second-class ground up toward the Rectory east face and past the Convent and Mosque notch; the brush is thick and the way is not obvious. The route has bolts right of the chimney that is right of Mazel Tov!.

ca_table_top_rock_pinch_it_or_reach_it.approach: From the north shore of Big Bear Lake, park where Greenway Drive meets Pioneer Lane and take the trails that wander up the hillside; the formations sit on the south-facing slope above. Table Top Rock is a hike uphill and west from Secret Spot Rock. The route is on the left side of the south face.

ca_taggers_chips_and_dip.approach: From the north shore of Big Bear Lake, park where Greenway Drive meets Pioneer Lane and take the trails that wander up the hillside; the formations sit on the south-facing slope above. Taggers is a short way east of Cockell's Dome, directly downhill and south of Lime-Aid. The route is on the right side of the buttress toe, where a bolt marks it.

ca_taggers_lightning_visit.approach: From the north shore of Big Bear Lake, park where Greenway Drive meets Pioneer Lane and take the trails that wander up the hillside; the formations sit on the south-facing slope above. Taggers is a short way east of Cockell's Dome, directly downhill and south of Lime-Aid. The route is on the left side of the west face.

ca_tanglewood_slab_fast_and_easy.approach: Park in the northwest-facing turnout on the north side of forest road 3N16, east of Holcomb Valley Campground. The slab is visible from the road a short walk to the north. The route is above and slightly right of the main slab.

ca_temple_of_doom_west_tower_arete_route.approach: Hike to the Church Domes. Temple of Doom is beyond the huge Mosque and Tower of Babel faces: scramble up the pass past them, then go east and south to the south face of a crag built of three towers. The route climbs the southeast arete of the West Tower, right of Black Jesus.

ca_temple_of_doom_west_tower_east_face_r.approach: Hike to the Church Domes. Temple of Doom is beyond the huge Mosque and Tower of Babel faces: scramble up the pass past them, then go east and south to the south face of a crag built of three towers. The route is on the east face of the West Tower, left of The Sinner.

ca_the_addams_family_cousin_itt.approach: Take the trail toward Dragonlance Wall and Voodoo Wall over the first ridge and across the seasonal creek. The Addams Family slab appears on your left roughly midway up the approach gully. The route is the only bolted line, in the center of the slab.

ca_the_egg_deviled_egg.approach: From the north shore of Big Bear Lake, park where Greenway Drive meets Pioneer Lane and take the trails that wander up the hillside; the formations sit on the south-facing slope above. The Egg is uphill and slightly northwest of Lime-Aid. The route is on the right side of the north face and starts from a downed tree at the base.

ca_the_epicenter_richter_scale.approach: From the north shore of Big Bear Lake, park where Greenway Drive meets Pioneer Lane and take the trails that wander up the hillside; the formations sit on the south-facing slope above. The Epicenter is uphill and northeast of Big Bubba. The route is in the center of the south face.

ca_venice_slab_barney_rubble.approach: From the Topanga Lookout trailhead hike down past the old lookout foundation; the top of the slab comes into view, and a little further along use trails drop to its base. The route is down and left from Pebbles; skirt the slab downhill, or work up the lowest slabs to a small level spot beside a big bush, where the bolt line begins.

ca_venice_slab_pebbles.approach: From the Topanga Lookout trailhead hike down past the old lookout foundation; the top of the slab comes into view, and a little further along use trails drop to its base. The route follows the newer bolt line on the far right side of the slab.

ca_west_face_16_ashes_to_ashes.approach: Park in the dirt pullout west of the Tuolumne store along Tioga Road and follow the trail past a creek bed and up the slabs; stay below the summit and work left along the base to Peanut Gallery, a black wall carrying a few bolts. From there a scramble over second- to third-class ground reaches the main climbs. The route follows a black streak just left of Orange Plasma.

ca_west_face_16_welcome_home.approach: Park in the dirt pullout west of the Tuolumne store along Tioga Road and follow the trail past a creek bed and up the slabs; stay below the summit and work left along the base to Peanut Gallery, a black wall carrying a few bolts. From there a scramble over second- to third-class ground reaches the main climbs. The route is just right of Orange Plasma, and the first bolt is within reach from the ledge.

co_a_bug_s_crag_aspen_in_chains.approach: Park at campsite number 9 in McCullough Gulch, return a short distance down the road to a gap in the aspens that gives onto the top of the crag. Work right and downhill, passing the aspen that has grown around some old chains, then keep going right and down to the base. Aspen In Chains is the tallest climb on this rock.

co_a_bug_s_crag_hornet_s_lair.approach: Park at campsite number 9 in McCullough Gulch, return a short distance down the road to a gap in the aspens that gives onto the top of the crag. Work right and downhill, passing the aspen that has grown around some old chains, then keep going right and down to the base. Hornet's Lair is up and to the right.

co_a_bug_s_crag_i_m_a_beautiful_butterfl.approach: Park at campsite number 9 in McCullough Gulch, return a short distance down the road to a gap in the aspens that gives onto the top of the crag. Work right and downhill, passing the aspen that has grown around some old chains, then keep going right and down to the base. “I’m a Beautiful Butterfly” sits on the face directly right of Aspen In Chains.

co_a_bug_s_crag_rosie_the_spider.approach: Park at campsite number 9 in McCullough Gulch, return a short distance down the road to a gap in the aspens that gives onto the top of the crag. Work right and downhill, passing the aspen that has grown around some old chains, then keep going right and down to the base. Rosie The Spider is high on the right side of the crag, starting left below the large aspen tree.

co_a_bug_s_crag_squirmy_wormy.approach: Park at campsite number 9 in McCullough Gulch, return a short distance down the road to a gap in the aspens that gives onto the top of the crag. Work right and downhill, passing the aspen that has grown around some old chains, then keep going right and down to the base. Squirmy Wormy lies to the left of Aspen In Chains, the tallest line here; it starts high on the left or from the first bolt of Aspen In Chains.

co_lincoln_lake_slabs_balisong.approach: Drive up the Mount Blue Sky (formerly Mount Evans) road past Lincoln Lake, the long lake on the left before Summit Lake. The slabs are the obvious rock features rising right beside the road, with small pullouts on the drop-off side at and after the corner where the road crosses above the last cliff. Balisong follows the painted bolts between Gettysburg Address and Pika, and can finish on either anchor.

co_mind_dump_angry_pika.approach: Take County Road 805 to the gate and park near it without blocking the road. Walk down the road past a cabin, then at the next creek sign bear left and go uphill to a talus field and the cliff; aim for the top of the mine tailings field. The crag faces north on Northstar Mountain. Angry Pika is the left of the two bolted routes in the middle of the crag.

co_mind_dump_climbing_in_khakis.approach: Take County Road 805 to the gate and park near it without blocking the road. Walk down the road past a cabin, then at the next creek sign bear left and go uphill to a talus field and the cliff; aim for the top of the mine tailings field. The crag faces north on Northstar Mountain. Climbing In Khakis is the right of the two bolted lines in the middle of the crag.

co_mind_dump_sprinkled_with_snow.approach: Take County Road 805 to the gate and park near it without blocking the road. Walk down the road past a cabin, then at the next creek sign bear left and go uphill to a talus field and the cliff; aim for the top of the mine tailings field. The crag faces north on Northstar Mountain. Sprinkled With Snow is on the far right, tucked behind trees so that you only spot it once you walk across.

co_mind_dump_there_is_something_in_the_w.approach: Take County Road 805 to the gate and park near it without blocking the road. Walk down the road past a cabin, then at the next creek sign bear left and go uphill to a talus field and the cliff; aim for the top of the mine tailings field. The crag faces north on Northstar Mountain. This route is on the far left of the crag and is the only vertical climbing on the wall.

co_sakkety_point_rose_s_cantina.approach: Although the cliffs lie within Arapaho National Forest, the simplest access crosses private property: with permission, walk south from the trailhead a little way inside the Latigo Ranch gate. The other way is to walk due east from the forest service road through the trees. Rose's Cantina starts downhill, on the climber's left, of Bless You.

co_sakkety_point_the_onion.approach: Although the cliffs lie within Arapaho National Forest, the simplest access crosses private property: with permission, walk south from the trailhead a little way inside the Latigo Ranch gate. The other way is to walk due east from the forest service road through the trees. The Onion is the leftmost route on the crag.

co_thunderdome_buttress_furiosa.approach: Furiosa begins a short way right of The Nose, with an easy two-bolt slab pitch reaching a bolted anchor on a grubby ledge, above which the main pitch uses cracks and then a pocketed face up and left.

co_thunderdome_buttress_juice.approach: Juice starts from the Master Blaster anchor: follow the ramp that angles left to the higher anchor on the right, atop the formation known as the Anvil. Reach the Master Blaster anchor by climbing Master Blaster, or by climbing Bartertown to its second ledge.

co_thunderdome_buttress_master_blaster.approach: Master Blaster starts on Bartertown. Climb Bartertown to its second ledge, where a two-bolt anchor serves this route, and begin from there; the first bolt is a little above the ledge.

co_thunderdome_buttress_road_warrior.approach: To reach the start, climb Master Blaster, or climb Bartertown to its second anchor up and to the right on the big ledge and then rappel the Road Warrior bolts down to the Master Blaster anchor. Road Warrior climbs the bolted line to the right of that anchor to the same anchor as Juice.

co_thunderdome_buttress_the_nose.approach: The Nose forms the middle of Thunderdome Buttress, and the route starts just above the approach trail. It climbs five bolts to a big ledge with a two-bolt anchor, which is the base for the overhanging corner routes above.

co_thunderdome_buttress_war_boys.approach: War Boys starts from the ledge anchor at the top of Furiosa's approach pitch: climb that pitch and belay there. The route is the left-facing overhanging rhyolite corner just right of Furiosa.

id_north_face_gunsight_peak_chore_of_enc.approach: There are two ways in. From the Priest Lake side, hike the Chimney trail in to Roothaan and then follow the ridge down toward Gunsight. The shorter way is to hike into Hunt Lake, swing around Gunsight's back-left side and traverse in under the north face. The basin under the face has room for tents and snowfield melt for water, and a cable between two trees serves for hanging food. To find the start, look for the arch at mid-face, then trace the diagonal crack that descends rightward from the arch's right-hand end; the climbing starts on the right half of the shallow corner system beneath it.

id_south_dome_the_brotherhood.approach: Park as for the Lion Creek water slides and pass through the concrete barricades, then look for cairns and rough paths down to the creek crossing. Past the crossing, a boulder-and-scree climb angling up and left, marked by a few cairns, takes you to the foot of the slabs. Slog up the talus and through the alders, following the cairns and yellow ribbons, until you step down to the southwest toe of the slab. The first bolt is a short way up from there, and the route sits to the right of The Lion King.

id_south_side_south_side_slab.approach: Park in the pullouts just outside The Gap on the east side, then continue up Arimo Road on foot. The climbs are on the south side of the road, and a small creek crossing is needed to reach them. Look for the clear slab facing east on the gap's south side.

mt_bud_wall_the_blues_riff.approach: Cross the meadow on the climbers trail, heading directly to the Lower Replica, the first big triangular cliff you meet. Trails to every other cliff at the crag fork from its base. Turn up and right, following the trail as it parallels the cliff to a small scree field between the Lower and Upper Replica. Cross it, follow the trail past the Upper Replica to another short scree field, and continue up the hill to the left. The first route you reach is Boy Scout Hand Grenade, and the rest are off a small ledge with a few trees further up the hill. Blues Riff is the leftmost line on the Bud Wall, just past the corner from Boy Scout Hand Grenade.

mt_denmark_chai_in_my_eye.approach: Cross the meadow on the climbers trail, heading directly to the Lower Replica, the first big triangular cliff you meet. Trails to every other cliff at the crag fork from its base. Rather than climbing the trail to the right, turn left across a small scree slide to the short cliff beneath the tall, roofed wall (Sweden). Love Your Shotgun is the first route you meet. Chai in my eye is on the cliff's left end, beyond a patch of nettles.

mt_lower_replica_colossus.approach: Cross the meadow on the climbers trail, heading directly to the Lower Replica, the first big triangular cliff you meet. Trails to every other cliff at the crag fork from its base. Colossus starts a bit left of the big gold streak that marks the middle of the wall; its first bolts are left of a distinct chert feature in the streak.

mt_lower_replica_lower_replica.approach: Cross the meadow on the climbers trail, heading directly to the Lower Replica, the first big triangular cliff you meet. Trails to every other cliff at the crag fork from its base. The first route you reach on the cliff is The Bowl of Heaven. This route is short, with a chain anchor.

mt_lower_replica_silver_trembling_hands.approach: Cross the meadow on the climbers trail, heading directly to the Lower Replica, the first big triangular cliff you meet. Trails to every other cliff at the crag fork from its base. Silver Trembling Hands starts along the right edge of the big gold streak at the wall's center.

mt_nomad_wall_the_the_view.approach: Cross the meadow on the climbers trail, heading directly to the Lower Replica, the first big triangular cliff you meet. Trails to every other cliff at the crag fork from its base. Take the trail left toward Sweden and Denmark, follow the faint trail to the ledge underneath Sweden's big roofs and continue beyond into the next scree drainage. Traverse the scree until the wall is visible up the hill to the right, then follow a narrow drainage up through a small constriction to the base. There may be a fixed hand line to aid a loose fourth-class section there. The approach is loose, so wear a helmet and watch your footing and rockfall. The View starts on the right side of the wall.

nh_01_main_wall_down_east_dickering.approach: Start at Old Man of the Mountain Historic Site, then hike the Greenleaf Trail up toward the AMC hut. Where the trail flattens, shortly before Eagle Pass, a small cairn on the left marks the start of a climbers' trail that heads uphill. Follow the climbers' trail, bearing left at every fork and staying left in the trees rather than going into the talus field on the right, to reach the Main Wall. The start is at the right-hand end of the stone patio, inside a short chimney. You can also reach the first-pitch anchor by walking the Right Flank ledge.

nh_01_main_wall_high_dollar_hounds.approach: Start at Old Man of the Mountain Historic Site, then hike the Greenleaf Trail up toward the AMC hut. Where the trail flattens, shortly before Eagle Pass, a small cairn on the left marks the start of a climbers' trail that heads uphill. Follow the climbers' trail, bearing left at every fork and staying left in the trees rather than going into the talus field on the right, to reach the Main Wall. It is the overhanging sport line next to Farewell Angelina, with Pin It To Win It on its other side, left of a birch tree where the trail levels off.

nh_03_the_dog_house_can_i_take_my_hounds.approach: Start at Old Man of the Mountain Historic Site, then hike the Greenleaf Trail up toward the AMC hut. Where the trail flattens, shortly before Eagle Pass, a small cairn on the left marks the start of a climbers' trail that heads uphill. Follow the climbers' trail a short way, take the right at the first fork, and follow that a very short way to reach the steep bolted wall of the Dog House. This route is the leftmost one at the crag and starts off a low rock step; the first bolts are over chossy rock, so a stick clip helps.

nh_03_the_dog_house_diamond_dogs.approach: Start at Old Man of the Mountain Historic Site, then hike the Greenleaf Trail up toward the AMC hut. Where the trail flattens, shortly before Eagle Pass, a small cairn on the left marks the start of a climbers' trail that heads uphill. Follow the climbers' trail a short way, take the right at the first fork, and follow that a very short way to reach the steep bolted wall of the Dog House. This is the route in the center of the crag, with a permadraw on the third bolt.

nh_03_the_dog_house_mr_sparkle.approach: Start at Old Man of the Mountain Historic Site, then hike the Greenleaf Trail up toward the AMC hut. Where the trail flattens, shortly before Eagle Pass, a small cairn on the left marks the start of a climbers' trail that heads uphill. Follow the climbers' trail a short way, take the right at the first fork, and follow that a very short way to reach the steep bolted wall of the Dog House. This is the crag's far-right route, and the only one lacking a permadraw.

nv_cleft_the_blue_eyes.approach: Drive the Hinkey Summit Road north out of Paradise Valley to a hairpin corner in an aspen grove, and park there or in a small pullout a little way back. The hiking trail, faint in places, starts at the hairpin and heads east toward the big cleft wall, crossing two drainages on the way to the base. Blue Eyes climbs the large headwall in the center of the Cleft. Walk left of Paiute Pockets and through a narrow slot to get to it. The climbing begins with a rightward traverse along a third-class ledge above a chossy overhang.

A small trail leaves to the left; take it to a service road, turn left, and follow the road as it steepens into a trail up to the buttress. Another way in is to ride the tram, take the Rock Springs Loop trail along the ridge toward Cody Peak, bear left onto a road, then right at the next junction onto what is the Rendezvous ski trail in winter; look on the right for a cairned climbers' trail that drops into the base of the buttress. The West Sector is reached after crossing the creek to the talus field and is the furthest left (west), flanked on its right by a steep gully; from the tram it is the first crag met on the way down into Rock Springs Canyon.

nv_hinkey_summit_basque_ing_in_the_sun.approach: Take the Hinkey Summit Road north from Paradise Valley toward the pass. Park in the narrow pullout on the road below the wall, or at the summit pass; the walk to the base of the climbing is very short. Basque-ing in the Sun is on the southern summit wall, which is almost its own wall, cut off from the other routes by some poor rock and a mound covered in shrubs. It starts in the lowest part of the prominent wall, a short way to the right of Evasive Maneuvers; the first bolt is just off the ground next to a large two-hand pocket.
nv_hinkey_summit_basque_ing_in_the_sun.descent_text: Rappelling the route is the only way down; there is no walk-off. The anchors have rap rings.

nv_hinkey_summit_belly_button.approach: Take the Hinkey Summit Road north from Paradise Valley toward the pass. Park in the narrow pullout on the road below the wall, or at the summit pass; the walk to the base of the climbing is very short. Belly Button is between Don't Call Me White and MuccLovin. Find the first bolt in a water streak a little above the ground, with easy climbing to reach it. The route leads into the large recessed cave halfway across the wall, or can continue past it to MuccLovin and Time Collapse.

nv_hinkey_summit_das_ntercling.approach: Take the Hinkey Summit Road north from Paradise Valley toward the pass. Park in the narrow pullout on the road below the wall, or at the summit pass; the walk to the base of the climbing is very short. From the base of Belly Button, follow the moderately steep gravel trail along the foot of the wall past MuccLovin to reach Das Untercling, which lies between MuccLovin and Lucky Pair a Dice. Its last bolt and anchor are shared with Lucky Pair a Dice.

nv_hinkey_summit_evasive_maneuvers.approach: Take the Hinkey Summit Road north from Paradise Valley toward the pass. Park in the narrow pullout on the road below the wall, or at the summit pass; the walk to the base of the climbing is very short. From Belly Button, follow the moderately steep gravel trail beside the wall, past MuccLovin, Das Untercling and Lucky Pair a Dice. Evasive Maneuvers is the final route on the wall, at the top of the gravel hill by the foot of the gully, a few feet left of it.

nv_hinkey_summit_lucky_pair_a_dice.approach: Take the Hinkey Summit Road north from Paradise Valley toward the pass. Park in the narrow pullout on the road below the wall, or at the summit pass; the walk to the base of the climbing is very short. From the base of Belly Button, follow the moderately steep gravel trail along the foot of the wall past MuccLovin and Das Untercling. Lucky Pair a Dice sits between Das Untercling and Evasive Maneuvers, and shares its last bolt and anchor with Das Untercling.

nv_hinkey_summit_mucclovin.approach: Take the Hinkey Summit Road north from Paradise Valley toward the pass. Park in the narrow pullout on the road below the wall, or at the summit pass; the walk to the base of the climbing is very short. MuccLovin starts between Belly Button and Das Untercling. Its anchors are shared with the top of Belly Button, on a comfortable ledge above and right of the cave.

nv_hinkey_summit_time_collapse.approach: Take the Hinkey Summit Road north from Paradise Valley toward the pass. Park in the narrow pullout on the road below the wall, or at the summit pass; the walk to the base of the climbing is very short. Time Collapse begins from a two-bolt belay on a ledge up and to the right of the big shallow cave, so get there by climbing MuccLovin or all of Belly Button.
nv_hinkey_summit_time_collapse.descent_text: Walk off: scramble easily up and left to the top, traverse right and a bit downhill to get off the back side, then head north past the big arch to the 4x4 road and follow it down to the parking area. You can instead rappel the route; the rappels finish in the cave and then reach the ground.

nv_honeycombs_deep_sea_diver.approach: Drive northeast past Hinkey Summit on Hinkey Summit Road, then park well off to the side in a wider part of the road. Hike northwest on cattle trails through the sagebrush and a small boulder field to reach the middle stretch of the wall. The first bolt is a short way up, with easy climbing to reach it and a flake near the first two bolts.

nv_iron_horse_run_a_mucca.approach: From the pullout on the Hinkey Summit Road, walk a short way up the road to a pair of cairns on the right marking where the trail begins. Traverse the hillsides north-northeast on the clearest cow trail, crossing Indian Creek about halfway at a spot marked by a stick-and-rock cairn and a large Y-shaped dead snag. Past the creek, follow cow and climber trails along the treeline northeast until Iron Horse comes into view; it can also be reached from the Cleft by a short, easy walk on cow trails. Run-A-Mucca is on the southern side of the wall, around the corner to the right of Yippee Ki Yay. It starts up a juggy water runnel, on the left-hand line of bolts, near where Liquid Gold starts.

nv_iron_horse_yippee_ki_yay.approach: From the pullout on the Hinkey Summit Road, walk a short way up the road to a pair of cairns on the right marking where the trail begins. Traverse the hillsides north-northeast on the clearest cow trail, crossing Indian Creek about halfway at a spot marked by a stick-and-rock cairn and a large Y-shaped dead snag. Past the creek, follow cow and climber trails along the treeline northeast until Iron Horse comes into view; it can also be reached from the Cleft by a short, easy walk on cow trails. Yippee Ki Yay is on the steeper, west-facing western part of the wall, which is heavily pocketed. The first bolt is reached by climbing the steeper rock beside the slab, on its right.

nv_rap_rock_unknown.approach: This is a roadside cliff in Lamoille Canyon. Beyond the girls camp, a roadside pullout lets you walk straight to the cliff. The route is a short bolted line.

nv_sport_rocks_a_k_a_flinstonehenge_side.approach: Park in the large lot on the right side of the road in Lamoille Canyon, just inside the canyon mouth. From the parking area, go straight to the nearest rock on the right. Sidewinder tracks the dark streak left of Unknown Route, on the first rock. The anchors are a little hidden at the top.

nv_sport_rocks_a_k_a_flinstonehenge_unkn.approach: Park in the large lot on the right side of the road in Lamoille Canyon, just inside the canyon mouth. It is on the first rock out from the parking area, immediately right of Sidewinder.

nv_sport_rocks_a_k_a_flinstonehenge_vaca.approach: Park in the large lot on the right side of the road in Lamoille Canyon, just inside the canyon mouth. The route is on the up-canyon side of the formation. It has chain anchors, and a stick clip for the first bolt is wise.

or_gym_wall_1_far_left.approach: Scorpion Buttress is in Britt Nichols County Park. After driving to the top of Callahan Road, come back down and park on the outside of the last switchback you passed on the way up, in the upper clear-cut, where a spur road is blocked with boulders. Walk the spur road almost to its end and take the obvious trail on the left, which runs downhill to the upper part of the buttress. From the top, either rappel in or take the steep switchbacking trail on the right down to the middle of West Gully. Gym Wall is the open steep slab on the left side as you go down the trail. This is the far-left route on the wall, and its top anchors are easy to reach.

Atonement sits beside the Madrone Crack and has a conspicuous hueco low on the route.
