or_lower_wall_angled_assassin.approach: Start at Anthony Lake and hike the Hoffer Lakes Trail to the higher of the two lakes. A small side valley runs southwest from it, holding the Upper and Lower Walls. Leaving the trail, work up and around the slabs along the lake's south shore into a meadow; the Lower Wall shows on the valley's right side beyond the meadow, and a faint path reaches its base. Angled Assassin pulls a roof to start and climbs a more featured, lower-angle face than the nearby Sticky Nails.

or_lower_wall_sticky_nails.approach: Start at Anthony Lake and hike the Hoffer Lakes Trail to the higher of the two lakes. Leaving the trail, work up and around the slabs along the lake's south shore into a meadow; the Lower Wall shows on the valley's right side beyond the meadow, and a faint path reaches its base. Sticky Nails is the left-most, uppermost route on the Lower Wall, on a thin face that gets thinner higher up.

or_panorama_point_more_bolts_than_balls.approach: Leave the upper climbers' camp on the trail that drops across Forest Service Road 850, then take the Lookout Ridge Trail until just short of the summit of the Panorama Point knoll. Close to the top a side trail on the left leads out onto Panorama Point, with Rabbit Ears in view to the south. Pick the side trail up again and follow it down the knoll's left, back side to the cliff base. The route is on a sub-buttress of Panorama Point.

vt_bat_cave_buttress_children_of_the_gra.approach: Bat Cave Buttress lies a little north of the Quartz Crack face and downhill. From Quartz Crack, follow the herd path north, losing a little height and continuing a few minutes beyond The Diagonal, until a low-angle slab with bolts runs off to the right of the path. You can also reach it by hiking up the herd path south from the ENT gully, or by climbing directly from the upper end of the notch parking lot, passing Biscuit. The route starts on that bolted slab where it touches down beside the herd path, shares its first two bolts with Steep Jugs, then breaks off right.

vt_bat_cave_buttress_the_residents.approach: Bat Cave Buttress lies a little north of the Quartz Crack face and downhill. From Quartz Crack, follow the herd path north, losing a little height and continuing a few minutes beyond The Diagonal, until a low-angle slab with bolts runs off to the right of the path. You can also come up the herd path from the ENT gully, or climb directly from the upper end of the notch parking lot, passing Biscuit. The route starts on the ledge of the buttress, at the overhang, on the face left of where Steep Jugs has its second pitch.

ut_exceeded_expectations_wall_exceeded_e.approach: Park on the large shoulder on the east side of the Little Cottonwood Canyon road, a short way beyond the Tanners Campground turnoff and before the bend. Across the road a trail starts behind the Tanners Slide Path highway sign; follow it (faint in places) to the drainage and walk up the gulch. The first pronounced gully on the left is Witches and Divas, and the east-facing Exceeded Expectations Wall stands on the right side of its mouth, with the shortest approach in the gulch. This is the far right route on the wall; the start is broken ground with loose dirt and rock. In winter and spring the gulch can slide, so check the avalanche forecast.

ut_exceeded_expectations_wall_pootie_tan.approach: Park on the large shoulder on the east side of the Little Cottonwood Canyon road, a short way beyond the Tanners Campground turnoff and before the bend. ut_upper_jungle_raj.approach: Drive past the Lower Jungle parking area and around the corner up the road to the marked Upper Jungle pullout. A short approach, marked by cairns, leads down to the crag. Raj starts as Monkey Bumps does, going to the ledge, then goes straight up the arete.

ut_lower_jungle_kaa.approach: Park at the Lower Jungle pullout, a flat rocky spot on the right of the road, and take the cairned trail that begins with a few big steps up and a built-up log crossing. The trail runs north along the foot of the cliff band through the Lower Jungle routes. Kaa is the short, steep wall between Dr. Livingstone, I Presume? and Man Next Door.

wy_the_mouth_of_the_clark_s_fork_milky_w.approach: Clark is north of Cody on Wyoming Highway 120, near the Montana line. Turn west at the Edelweiss Restaurant onto Canyon Road 1AB and follow it to the mouth of Clark's Fork Canyon, where the north massif is hard to miss. From the highway, cross a BLM fence and walk a short way to the routes. Milky Way is the second route from the left.

wy_the_mouth_of_the_clark_s_fork_powder_.approach: Clark is north of Cody on Wyoming Highway 120, near the Montana line. Turn west at the Edelweiss Restaurant onto Canyon Road 1AB and follow it to the mouth of Clark's Fork Canyon, where the north massif is hard to miss. From the highway, cross a BLM fence and walk a short way to the routes. Powder Puff is the leftmost line on the Milky Slab, the clean grey slab low and to the left in the Mouth area.

wy_island_the_climbs_boomstick.approach: Park in the climbers' lot on the north side of the highway at the west end of Shoshone Canyon, between the second short tunnel and the long tunnel. The Island is the plug of granite directly in front of the lot, only seconds away. Boomstick starts a short way right of In With The New, in the corner, and follows the face just left of the corner.

wy_island_the_climbs_crimp_master_5000_a.approach: Park in the climbers' lot on the north side of the highway at the west end of Shoshone Canyon, between the second short tunnel and the long tunnel. The Island is the plug of granite directly in front of the lot, only seconds away. Crimp Master 5000 lies between Pea Green Limousine on its left and Big Ben on its right.

wy_island_the_climbs_irma.approach: Park in the climbers' lot on the north side of the highway at the west end of Shoshone Canyon, between the second short tunnel and the long tunnel. The Island is the plug of granite directly in front of the lot, only seconds away. Irma's slab start is immediately right of Bruce's Crack.

wy_island_the_climbs_pea_green_limousine.approach: Park in the climbers' lot on the north side of the highway at the west end of Shoshone Canyon, between the second short tunnel and the long tunnel. The Island is the plug of granite directly in front of the lot, only seconds away. Pea Green Limousine sits between Mind Games and Crimp Master 5000.

wy_upper_blacktail_butte_sthank_o.approach: Starting at the Blacktail lot, head south on the well-developed trail as it climbs and crosses a small creek; after that, look for a trail on the left through the talus. It leads to the Middle Wall and continues to the Upper Wall. stHank-O is just left of Blitzkrieg and right of a choss gully, following an obvious black and blue streak.
